title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 55
statement: A sequence of positive integers is given by \(a_{1}=1\) and \(a_{n}=\operatorname{gcd}\left(a_{n-1}, n\right)+1\) for \(n>1\). Calculate \(a_{2002}\).

solutions.text: 3. It is readily seen by induction that \(a_{n} \leq n\) for all \(n\). On the other hand, \(a_{1999}\) is one greater than a divisor of 1999. Since 1999 is prime, we have \(a_{1999}=2\) or 2000; the latter is not possible since \(2000>1999\), so we have \(a_{1999}=2\). Now we straightforwardly compute \(a_{2000}=3, a_{2001}=4\), and \(a_{2002}=3\).
